subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what trigger plus local editor/temp-file safety contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation surface is clear, but launching `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR` and persisting prompt drafts to disk is a product and security boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with a maintainer-approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold For UX Choice
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose the shortcut or slash-command model and resolve the Ctrl+E/Ctrl+G conflict.

options.title: Decline External Process Handoff
options.body: Narrow or close the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing, a larger composer, or another non-process-based editing path.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with a maintainer-approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed this exact issue and have the strongest available TUI docs, keybinding, and pi-tui alignment history.
